content.text:
I’d make **`/` the landing page and move the font library to `/fonts/`**. That gives Glypherie a clear introduction and regular users a URL they can bookmark directly.

Your current app already has distinct font and palette routes, so the structure would stay simple:

| URL | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/` | Introduction and quick start |
| `/fonts/` | Font library |
| `/font/<id>/` | Existing font preview |
| `/font/<id>/variant/<id>/` | Existing saved variant |
| `/palettes/` | Existing palette lab |

All paths would remain relative to the configured hosting prefix, including on GitHub Pages.

For the landing itself, I’d use a **short, illustrated project introduction** with:

- A sentence explaining what Glypherie does and who it helps.
- One representative preview showing its purpose.
- A prominent **Open font library** button.
- A three-step explanation: import a font → adjust a preview → save or export.
- A brief explanation of browser-local storage and links to source and documentation.

In navigation, the **Glypherie logo would lead to `/`**, while **Fonts** would always lead to `/fonts/`. I’d keep those destinations consistent across visits.

Both approaches have precedents: [Squoosh](https://squoosh.app/) combines its tool and introduction at the root; [Penpot](https://penpot.app/) gives its introduction a separate entrance to the application. For Glypherie, I’d choose the latter separation, within the same site.

The tradeoff is one extra click from the homepage. A direct `/fonts/` bookmark handles everyday use, while `/` becomes a useful link to share when introducing the project.
